rawRecord.EXPERIMENTAL_ai_generated_description: This Kali Linux MCP server by Ethan Blair provides remote access to penetration testing and security assessment tools through a client-server architecture, with the server component running on a Kali Linux system and exposing security tools via Flask REST API endpoints. Built with Python and featuring a FastMCP client that communicates with the Kali server, it offers tools for network scanning (nmap), web directory enumeration (gobuster, dirb), vulnerability assessment (nikto, wpscan), SQL injection testing (sqlmap), password cracking (hydra, john), exploitation frameworks (metasploit), and system enumeration (enum4linux), plus arbitrary command execution capabilities. The implementation includes robust command execution with timeout handling, threading for real-time output capture, health monitoring for tool availability, and configurable request timeouts, making it valuable for security professionals conducting remote penetration tests, red team exercises, and security assessments where they need AI-assisted tool orchestration and centralized access to Kali Linux security utilities from non-Kali systems.
